subject: Halden update for the partner meeting
body:
Hi Elliot,

Thanks again for having us on Thursday, and to Sam and your hardware EIR for the hard questions. The team came out of it energized. As promised, here's a quick update with the latest numbers for your memo ahead of the partner meeting.

Where we are:
- ARR of $7.9M, growing ~40% year over year
- 12 paying customers across the US and Europe
- Gross margin of 71% blended (83% on software)
- Over 20 months of runway at current burn, so we're raising from a position of strength
- Deployed at 1,000+ intersections

On results, our adaptive signal timing has cut intersection delay by 18% across our pilots, and Tacoma has already expanded to the full Pacific Ave corridor. Our incident detection catches crashes, stalled vehicles and wrong-way drivers in under 5 seconds, which is a big deal for TMCs that today mostly hear about incidents from 911 calls (in Dayton it was 6.5 minutes on average before us).

I also wanted to say a bit more about the technology since it came up a lot on Thursday. What makes Halden work is that everything runs on the edge: the HX-4 sits in the signal cabinet and runs our detection, tracking and incident models on the cameras the city already owns, so we only send compressed metadata and occasional keyframes upstream, about 180 kbps per camera, which is why we can run over LTE where competitors need fiber, and why our hosting costs stay low as we scale. We have patents on the adaptive signal timing approach and on edge incident detection, and the low-bandwidth codec is pending, so we think the moat is real and gets deeper as we add more cities and more data, and HX-5 next year brings the hardware cost down meaningfully while adding streams, which helps margins and makes the hardware-as-a-service model you asked about the natural default going forward.

On concentration, I know it's the main question. Our largest contract (regional security services, through a procurement intermediary) is still a big part of revenue, but municipal is growing much faster and we're actively diversifying, with a board target to get it under 60% by end of 2027.

We're raising $25M to scale R&D, go-to-market in the US and Europe, and HX-5. Priya is pulling the cohort data and downside case you asked for, and Tom will send the Chattanooga SOW.

Happy to jump on a call Monday if anything would help before the meeting.

Best,
Dana
